meta.audience: The people of Zarahemla, from the city wall
meta.location: The wall of the city of Zarahemla
principles: A prophet sent back after being refused

world_behind.title: The preacher is a Lamanite
world_behind.text: Verse 2 names him and his people, and verse 1 has just said the Lamanites keep the law of Moses strictly while the Nephites do not.

world_behind.title: He was already finished and leaving
world_behind.text: Verses 2 and 3 have him cast out, headed home, and turned around by the voice of the Lord.

world_behind.title: The wall is a workaround
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says they would not let him into the city, so he climbed the wall and preached from there.

world_behind.title: The four hundred years are dated
world_behind.text: Verses 5 and 9 give the interval twice, and verse 10 says men of the fourth generation among his enemies will see the destruction.

world_behind.title: Zarahemla is standing on borrowed time
world_behind.text: Verses 12 and 13 say the righteous are the reason it is spared, and verse 14 gives the moment it will be ripe: when they cast the righteous out.

world_behind.title: The curse on riches is stated in full
world_behind.text: Verses 18 through 23 and 31 through 36 describe treasures that cannot be found and tools that vanish overnight.

world_behind.title: The lament is written out in advance
world_behind.text: Verses 33 through 37 give the words the people will say, and verse 37 ends them mid-prayer.

words.text: News, especially good news. The record uses the word twenty-two times and the King James Bible forty-six. Verse 7 has an angel bringing glad tidings to Samuel, who was sent to pass them on and was refused.
Clothing, in the record usually costly clothing. The word occurs fourteen times, often as a marker of pride, as at Alma 1:6 and Alma 4:6. Verse 28 has it given to a man who says all is well.
Turned away from what is right. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible twenty. Samuel pairs it with hardened and stiffnecked in a single address.
Set alight. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible sixty-six, nearly always of anger. Verse 30 says the anger is already kindled, in the past tense.
Unable to be held. The record uses the word four times, three of them in this chapter and one at Mormon 1:18, where Mormon reports it happening. The King James Bible has it three times, of paths.
Evil spirits. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, inside the lament Samuel puts in their mouths.

phrases.term: There was one Samuel, a Lamanite, came into the land of Zarahemla
phrases.text: The record introduces its only named Lamanite prophet in a single clause. Verse 1 has already reported which people was keeping the law.

phrases.term: He went and got upon the wall thereof
phrases.text: The improvisation that makes the chapter possible. Shut out of the city, he preaches from its boundary.

phrases.term: Four hundred years pass not away save the sword of justice falleth upon this people
phrases.text: The interval given at the start of the sermon. Verse 9 repeats it, and Mormon writes the abridgment from the far side of it.

phrases.term: It is because of those who are righteous that it is saved
phrases.text: The reason the city still stands. Verse 13 says fire from heaven would otherwise have come down.

phrases.term: When ye shall cast out the righteous from among you, then shall ye be ripe for destruction
phrases.text: The condition that ends the reprieve. The city's protection is a group of people it can decide to expel.

phrases.term: Whoso shall hide up treasures in the earth shall find them again no more
phrases.text: The curse stated as law. Helaman 12:18 had given the principle, and this verse extends it over the whole land.

phrases.term: Ye do always remember your riches, not to thank the Lord your God for them
phrases.text: The distinction between remembering a thing and remembering its source. Verse 22 lists what fills the space instead: pride, boasting, envyings, strifes, malice, persecutions, murders.

phrases.term: If our days had been in the days of our fathers of old, we would not have slain the prophets
phrases.text: The claim Samuel quotes back at them. Verse 26 answers it by describing what they do to a prophet who is standing in front of them.

phrases.term: Because he speaketh flattering words unto you, and he saith that all is well
phrases.text: The test the people actually use. A man who says there is no iniquity gets gold, silver, and costly apparel.

phrases.term: He curseth your riches, that they become slippery, that ye cannot hold them
phrases.text: The image the chapter is remembered by. Mormon 1:18 reports it as an ordinary fact of daily life three centuries later.

phrases.term: Ye have sought for happiness in doing iniquity
phrases.text: The summary of the whole failure. Alma 41:10 had put it in four words to his own son.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: Sent back
verses.text: In the eighty-sixth year the Nephites remain in great wickedness while the Lamanites keep the commandments strictly. Samuel, a Lamanite, comes to Zarahemla, preaches repentance many days, is cast out, and starts home. The voice of the Lord sends him back to prophesy whatever comes into his heart. Refused entry, he climbs the wall and cries out that the sword of justice hangs over the people and will fall within four hundred years, and that only repentance and faith in Christ can save them. An angel had brought him glad tidings to deliver, and they would not receive him.

verses.label: v. 8–11
verses.title: The terms
verses.text: Unless they repent, the Lord will take away his word, withdraw his Spirit, suffer them no longer, and turn their brethren's hearts against them. Within four hundred years he will smite them with sword, famine, and pestilence, and men of the fourth generation among their enemies will live to see the destruction. If they repent, the anger turns away.

verses.label: v. 12–17
verses.title: Wo on the cities
verses.text: Wo to Zarahemla, saved only because of the righteous in it, though the more part will harden their hearts. The repentant will be spared, and without the righteous, fire would come down from heaven. When they cast the righteous out, they will be ripe. Wo also to Gideon and to all the cities round about, and a curse comes on the land itself.

verses.label: v. 18–23
verses.title: The curse on treasure
verses.text: Whoever hides treasure in the earth will not find it again, except a righteous man who hides it up unto the Lord. Those who do not are cursed, and so is the treasure, and none shall redeem it. The day comes when they will hide their treasures because their hearts are set on riches and they are fleeing enemies. They are cursed because of their riches, and their riches with them, since they remember the riches and not the giver.

verses.label: v. 24–28
verses.title: How they treat prophets
verses.text: Wo for casting out, mocking, stoning, and slaying the prophets as men did of old. They say that in their fathers' day they would not have done it. Samuel says they are worse: a prophet who names their sins is called false and of the devil, while a man who says do what you like and all is well is lifted up, given gold and silver and costly apparel, and called a prophet.

verses.label: v. 29–37
verses.title: Slippery
verses.text: He calls them wicked, perverse, hardened, and stiffnecked, and asks how long they will be led by blind guides and choose darkness. The anger is already kindled and the land already cursed. Their riches will become slippery and unholdable, and in their poverty they will cry in vain, weep, and howl. He writes their lament for them: a wish they had repented, tools gone by morning, swords missing on the day of battle, treasures slipped away, and a sense of being surrounded by demons.

verses.label: v. 38–39
verses.title: Too late, and a prayer
verses.text: Their days of probation are past, the day of salvation procrastinated until it is everlastingly too late, and they have sought happiness in doing iniquity, which is contrary to righteousness. Samuel wishes they would hear him and prays that the anger be turned away and that they repent and be saved.

chapter.title: The prophet was already leaving
chapter.text: Verses 2 and 3 have him finished and turned around. Everything in the chapter happens after the point where a reasonable person would have gone home.

chapter.title: The wall is the sermon's setting and its argument
chapter.text: He is outside because they put him there, and he preaches from the boundary of a city he was not allowed into.

chapter.title: A Lamanite preaches to the Nephites
chapter.text: Verse 1 sets up the reversal Helaman 6 had already reported. The messenger's identity is part of the message.

chapter.title: The city is spared for its minority
chapter.text: Verses 12 through 14 make the righteous the reason it stands and their expulsion the moment it falls. Genesis 18 had put the same arithmetic to Abraham.

chapter.title: The test for a prophet is comfort
chapter.text: Verses 26 through 28 describe people who reward the man who says all is well. Samuel names the mechanism rather than only the outcome.

chapter.title: The curse works on holding, not on having
chapter.text: Verse 31 does not take the riches away; it makes them impossible to keep. Mormon 1:18 reports tools and treasures vanishing as normal life.

chapter.title: The lament is supplied in advance
chapter.text: Verses 33 through 37 are written in their future voice. Samuel gives them the words and tells them this will be their language.

chapter.title: He ends with a prayer for them
chapter.text: Verse 39 follows the sentence that it is everlastingly too late. The chapter closes on the wish rather than on the verdict.

applications.title: Go back when you are sent back
applications.text: He had preached, been refused, and started home, and the instruction was to return. A closed door is sometimes not the end of the assignment.

applications.title: Preach from the wall
applications.text: Barred from the city, he used its boundary. When the ordinary access is denied, look for the position that still lets the work happen.

applications.title: Watch who you reward for telling you things
applications.text: They paid the man who said all is well. Notice which messengers you fund and which you resent.

applications.title: Hold your holdings loosely
applications.text: The curse was on keeping rather than on having. Anything you are counting on to stay put is worth examining while it is still in hand.

questions.text: What was I about to give up on that I have been told to resume?
Who is keeping the place I live standing?
Do I remember the gift or the giver?
What would I claim I would have done in someone else's era?
Whose true words about me have I called unfair?
What comfortable voice am I paying for?
What would I say if I lost what I am holding onto now?

entries.head: Hel. 12:18

anchor.quote: whoso shall hide up treasures in the earth shall find them again no more

entries.reason: the principle stated as commentary before it became prophecy

targets.quote: if a man hide up a treasure in the earth,
targets.verse_text: And behold, if a man hide up a treasure in the earth, and the Lord shall say—Let it be accursed, because of the iniquity of him who hath hid it up—behold, it shall be accursed.
targets.markdown: And behold, **if a man hide up a treasure in the earth**, and the Lord shall say—Let it be accursed, because of the iniquity of him who hath hid it up—behold, it shall be accursed.

entries.head: Hel. 6:1

anchor.quote: the Lamanites did observe strictly to keep the commandments of God

entries.reason: the reversal reported seven chapters earlier as accomplished fact

targets.quote: their righteousness did exceed that of the Nephites,
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that when the sixty and second year of the reign of the judges had ended, all these things had happened and the Lamanites had become, the more part of them, a righteous people, insomuch that their righteousness did exceed that of the Nephites, because of their firmness and their steadiness in the faith.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that when the sixty and second year of the reign of the judges had ended, all these things had happened and the Lamanites had become, the more part of them, a righteous people, insomuch that **their righteousness did exceed that of the Nephites**, because of their firmness and their steadiness in the faith.

entries.head: Hel. 16:2

anchor.quote: he went and got upon the wall thereof

entries.reason: the stones and arrows that could not reach him there

targets.quote: they cast stones at him upon the wall, and also many shot arrows at him
targets.verse_text: But as many as there were who did not believe in the words of Samuel were angry with him; and they cast stones at him upon the wall, and also many shot arrows at him as he stood upon the wall; but the Spirit of the Lord was with him, insomuch that they could not hit him with their stones neither with their arrows.
targets.markdown: But as many as there were who did not believe in the words of Samuel were angry with him; and **they cast stones at him upon the wall, and also many shot arrows at him** as he stood upon the wall; but the Spirit of the Lord was with him, insomuch that they could not hit him with their stones neither with their arrows.

entries.head: Hel. 12:2

anchor.quote: Ye do not remember the Lord your God in the things with which he hath blessed you

entries.reason: Mormon on the moment prosperity turns into forgetting

targets.quote: then is the time that they do harden their hearts,
targets.verse_text: Yea, and we may see at the very time when he doth prosper his people, yea, in the increase of their fields, their flocks and their herds, and in gold, and in silver, and in all manner of precious things of every kind and art; sparing their lives, and delivering them out of the hands of their enemies; softening the hearts of their enemies that they should not declare wars against them; yea, and in fine, doing all things for the welfare and happiness of his people; yea, then is the time that they do harden their hearts, and do forget the Lord their God, and do trample under their feet the Holy One—yea, and this because of their ease, and their exceedingly great prosperity.

anchor.quote: he curseth your riches, that they become slippery, that ye cannot hold them

entries.reason: Mormon reporting the curse as ordinary life, three centuries later

targets.quote: they became slippery, because the Lord had cursed the land,
targets.verse_text: And these Gadianton robbers, who were among the Lamanites, did infest the land, insomuch that the inhabitants thereof began to hide up their treasures in the earth; and they became slippery, because the Lord had cursed the land, that they could not hold them, nor retain them again.

entries.head: Alma 34:33

anchor.quote: ye have procrastinated the day of your salvation

entries.reason: Amulek using the same verb, and giving the reason

targets.quote: I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance
targets.verse_text: And now, as I said unto you before, as ye have had so many witnesses, therefore, I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end; for after this day of life, which is given us to prepare for eternity, behold, if we do not improve our time while in this life, then cometh the night of darkness wherein there can be no labor performed.
targets.markdown: And now, as I said unto you before, as ye have had so many witnesses, therefore, **I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance** until the end; for after this day of life, which is given us to prepare for eternity, behold, if we do not improve our time while in this life, then cometh the night of darkness wherein there can be no labor performed.

entries.head: Alma 41:10

anchor.quote: ye have sought for happiness in doing iniquity

entries.reason: Alma putting the same claim to his son in four words

targets.verse_text: Do not suppose, because it has been spoken concerning restoration, that ye shall be restored from sin to happiness. Behold, I say unto you, wickedness never was happiness.
targets.markdown: Do not suppose, because it has been spoken concerning restoration, that ye shall be restored from sin to happiness. Behold, I say unto you, **wickedness never was happiness**.

entries.head: 2 Ne. 28:21

anchor.quote: he saith that all is well

entries.reason: Nephi describing the same sentence as a device for lulling

targets.quote: they will say: All is well in Zion;
targets.verse_text: And others will he pacify, and lull them away into carnal security, that they will say: All is well in Zion; yea, Zion prospereth, all is well—and thus the devil cheateth their souls, and leadeth them away carefully down to hell.

anchor.quote: If our days had been in the days of our fathers of old, we would not have slain the prophets

entries.reason: the same claim, quoted back at the same kind of audience

targets.quote: If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
targets.verse_text: And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
targets.markdown: And say, **If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets**.
